sanskrit: imāñ śakunikān rājan hanti vaitaṃsiko yathā etad rūpam adharmasya bhūteṣu ca vihiṃsatām
english: Just as a fowler kills these birds, O king, so does one who harms living beings — this is the very form of unrighteousness among those who do violence to creatures.

sanskrit: kāmāl lobhāc ca dharmasya pravṛttiṃ yo na paśyati sa vadhyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ pretya ceha ca durmatiḥ
english: He who, out of desire and greed, does not perceive the operation of dharma — that evil-minded one is fit to be slain by all living beings, both in the next world and in this one.

sanskrit: vyaktaṃ te vidito rājann artho dravyaparigrahaḥ prakṛtiṃ cāpi vetthāsya vikṛtiṃ cāpi bhūyasīm
english: Clearly, O king, you know the meaning of the acquisition of wealth; you know its nature and its many corruptions as well.

sanskrit: tasya nāśaṃ vināśaṃ vā jarayā maraṇena vā anartham iti manyante so 'yam asmāsu vartate
english: Its loss or destruction — whether by old age or death — is considered a misfortune; and that misfortune now abides with us.

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ ca pañcānāṃ manaso hṛdayasya ca viṣaye vartamānānāṃ yā prītir upajāyate sa kāma iti me buddhiḥ karmaṇāṃ phalam uttamam
english: The delight that arises from the objects of the five senses, the mind, and the heart — that, in my understanding, is desire (kāma), and it is the highest fruit of action.

sanskrit: evam eva pṛthag dṛṣṭvā dharmārthau kāmam eva ca na dharmapara eva syān na cārthaparamo naraḥ na kāmaparamo vā syāt sarvān seveta sarvadā
english: Having thus separately observed dharma, artha, and kāma, a man should not be devoted solely to dharma, nor solely to artha, nor solely to kāma — he should always pursue all three.

sanskrit: dharmaṃ pūrvaṃ dhanaṃ madhye jaghanye kāmam ācaret ahany anucared evam eṣa śāstrakṛto vidhiḥ
english: One should practise dharma in the morning, wealth in the midday, and pleasure in the evening — this, day by day, is the rule laid down by the scriptures.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ pūrvaṃ dhanaṃ madhye jaghanye dharmam ācaret vayasy anucared evam eṣa śāstrakṛto vidhiḥ
english: In youth one should practise pleasure first, wealth in the middle years, and dharma in old age — such, at each stage of life, is the rule prescribed by the scriptures.

sanskrit: dharmaṃ cārthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca yathāvad vadatāṃ vara vibhajya kāle kālajñaḥ sarvān seveta paṇḍitaḥ
english: The wise man, best among those who speak rightly about dharma, artha, and kāma, knowing the proper time, should apportion and pursue all three in their proper seasons.

sanskrit: mokṣo vā paramaṃ śreya eṣa rājan sukhārthinām prāptir vā buddhim āsthāya sopāyaṃ kurunandana
english: Liberation is the highest good for those who seek happiness, O king; or else, O joy of the Kurus, one should attain it by applying intelligence together with the proper means.

sanskrit: tad vāśu kriyatāṃ rājan prāptir vāpy adhigamyatām jīvitaṃ hy āturasyeva duḥkham antaravartinaḥ
english: Therefore, O king, let this be done quickly, or let attainment be achieved; for the life of one trapped in affliction is like the life of a sick man — all suffering.

sanskrit: viditaś caiva te dharmaḥ satataṃ caritaś ca te jānate tvayi śaṃsanti suhṛdaḥ karmacodanām
english: Dharma is known to you and you have ever practised it; your friends, who know you, praise and urge you to action.

sanskrit: dānaṃ yajñaḥ satāṃ pūjā vedadhāraṇam ārjavam eṣa dharmaḥ paro rājan phalavān pretya ceha ca
english: Giving, sacrifice, honouring the good, preserving the Vedas, and uprightness — this is the highest dharma, O king, and it bears fruit both here and in the hereafter.

sanskrit: eṣa nārthavihīnena śakyo rājan niṣevitum akhilāḥ puruṣavyāghra guṇāḥ syur yady apītare
english: This cannot be practised by one devoid of wealth, O king; and all the other virtues too, O tiger among men, would be complete only if one has the means.

sanskrit: dharmamūlaṃ jagad rājan nānyad dharmād viśiṣyate dharmaś cārthena mahatā śakyo rājan niṣevitum
english: The world is rooted in dharma, O king; nothing is superior to dharma; and dharma, O king, can only be practised through great wealth.

sanskrit: na cārtho bhaikṣacaryeṇa nāpi klaibyena karhi cit vettuṃ śakyaḥ sadā rājan kevalaṃ dharmabuddhinā
english: Wealth cannot be acquired by begging, nor by cowardice, nor at any time by the mind of one who thinks only of dharma, O king.

sanskrit: pratiṣiddhā hi te yācñā yayā sidhyati vai dvijaḥ tejasaivārthalipsāyāṃ yatasva puruṣarṣabha
english: For you, begging — by which a brahmin may prosper — is forbidden; strive therefore to acquire wealth through your own energy alone, O bull among men.

sanskrit: bhaikṣacaryā na vihitā na ca viṭśūdrajīvikā kṣatriyasya viśeṣeṇa dharmas tu balam aurasam
english: Begging is not prescribed for a kshatriya, nor is the livelihood of a vaishya or shudra; for a kshatriya especially, dharma lies in his own innate strength.

sanskrit: udāram eva vidvāṃso dharmaṃ prāhur manīṣiṇaḥ udāraṃ pratipadyasva nāvare sthātum arhasi
english: The wise and learned call only the noble path dharma; adopt the noble course — you should not remain at a lesser level.

sanskrit: anubudhyasva rājendra vettha dharmān sanātanān krūrakarmābhijāto 'si yasmād udvijate janaḥ
english: Understand well, O lord of kings; you know the eternal laws of dharma. You were born to perform fierce deeds, before which people tremble.

sanskrit: prajāpālanasaṃbhūtaṃ phalaṃ tava na garhitam eṣa te vihito rājan dhātrā dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: The fruit arising from the protection of subjects is not blameworthy for you; this eternal dharma, O king, has been ordained for you by the Creator.

sanskrit: tasmād vicalitaḥ pārtha loke hāsyaṃ gamiṣyasi svadharmād dhi manuṣyāṇāṃ calanaṃ na praśasyate
english: Therefore, O Pārtha, if you deviate from this you will become a laughingstock in the world; for deviation from one's own dharma is not praised among men.

sanskrit: sa kṣātraṃ hṛdayaṃ kṛtvā tyaktvedaṃ śithilaṃ manaḥ vīryam āsthāya kaunteya dhuram udvaha dhuryavat
english: Make your heart that of a kshatriya; cast off this slackness of mind; relying on your valour, O son of Kuntī, bear the yoke like a draught-ox.

sanskrit: na hi kevaladharmātmā pṛthivīṃ jātu kaś cana pārthivo vyajayad rājan na bhūtiṃ na punaḥ śriyam
english: Never did any king conquer the earth, O king, by being devoted to dharma alone, nor did he achieve prosperity, nor recover royal fortune.

sanskrit: jihvāṃ dattvā bahūnāṃ hi kṣudrāṇāṃ lubdhacetasām nikṛtyā labhate rājyam āhāram iva śalyakaḥ
english: Indeed, by surrendering himself as prey to many petty and greedy minds, one obtains a kingdom through cunning, just as the porcupine obtains its food.

sanskrit: bhrātaraḥ pūrvajātāś ca susamṛddhāś ca sarvaśaḥ nikṛtyā nirjitā devair asurāḥ pāṇḍavarṣabha
english: Even the asuras — elder-born and vastly prosperous in every way — were completely defeated by the gods through cunning strategy, O bull of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: evaṃ balavataḥ sarvam iti buddhvā mahīpate jahi śatrūn mahābāho parāṃ nikṛtim āsthitaḥ
english: Knowing thus that everything belongs to the strong, O lord of the earth, slay your enemies, O mighty-armed one, by resorting to consummate strategy.

sanskrit: na hy arjunasamaḥ kaś cid yudhi yoddhā dhanurdharaḥ bhavitā vā pumān kaś cin matsamo vā gadādharaḥ
english: There is no warrior in battle equal to Arjuna among bowmen, nor will there ever be; and no man is or will be my equal as a wielder of the mace.

sanskrit: sattvena kurute yuddhaṃ rājan subalavān api na pramāṇena notsāhāt sattvastho bhava pāṇḍava
english: Even a man of great strength wages war through courage of spirit, O king, not through mere size, not through enthusiasm alone — be grounded in spirit, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: sattvaṃ hi mūlam arthasya vitathaṃ yad ato 'nyathā na tu prasaktaṃ bhavati vṛkṣacchāyeva haimanī
english: For courage of spirit is the root of all prosperity; what is otherwise is false; it does not endure, just as the shade of a tree in winter does not persist.

sanskrit: arthatyāgo hi kāryaḥ syād arthaṃ śreyāṃsam icchatā bījaupamyena kaunteya mā te bhūd atra saṃśayaḥ
english: One who desires greater wealth must give up lesser wealth — by the analogy of the seed, O son of Kuntī; let there be no doubt in you on this point.

sanskrit: arthena tu samo 'nartho yatra labhyeta nodayaḥ na tatra vipaṇaḥ kāryaḥ kharakaṇḍūyitaṃ hi tat
english: But where, by spending wealth, only equal wealth ��� and no increase — would be obtained, no transaction should be made there; that would be mere futile scratching like a donkey.

sanskrit: evam eva manuṣyendra dharmaṃ tyaktvālpakaṃ naraḥ bṛhantaṃ dharmam āpnoti sa buddha iti niścitaḥ
english: In the same way, O lord of men, a man who gives up a lesser dharma gains a greater dharma; he is surely to be considered wise.

sanskrit: amitraṃ mitrasaṃpannaṃ mitrair bhindanti paṇḍitāḥ bhinnair mitraiḥ parityaktaṃ durbalaṃ kurute vaśe
english: The wise sow division among an enemy's allies; the enemy, deserted by his divided allies, is weakened and brought under control.

sanskrit: sattvena kurute yuddhaṃ rājan subalavān api nodyamena na hotrābhiḥ sarvāḥ svīkurute prajāḥ
english: Even a very powerful man wages war through spirit, O king; not through exertion alone, nor through sacrificial offerings, does one bring all subjects under one's sway.

sanskrit: sarvathā saṃhatair eva durbalair balavān api amitraḥ śakyate hantuṃ madhuhā bhramarair iva
english: In every way, even a powerful enemy can be slain by weak ones acting in concert — just as a honey-bee is killed by a swarm of other bees.

sanskrit: yathā rājan prajāḥ sarvāḥ sūryaḥ pāti gabhastibhiḥ atti caiva tathaiva tvaṃ savituḥ sadṛśo bhava
english: Just as the sun, O king, both nourishes and consumes all subjects with its rays, so too be you like the sun.

sanskrit: etad dhy api tapo rājan purāṇam iti naḥ śrutam vidhinā pālanaṃ bhūmer yat kṛtaṃ naḥ pitāmahaiḥ
english: This too is an ancient austerity, as we have heard, O king — the dutiful protection of the earth as our forefathers performed it.

sanskrit: apeyāt kila bhāḥ sūryāl lakṣmīś candramasas tathā iti loko vyavasito dṛṣṭvemāṃ bhavato vyathām
english: It is said that the radiance might depart from the sun and Lakṣmī from the moon — thus the world concludes upon seeing your present distress.

sanskrit: bhavataś ca praśaṃsābhir nindābhir itarasya ca kathāyuktāḥ pariṣadaḥ pṛthag rājan samāgatāḥ
english: Assemblies filled with talk — praise of you and reproach of the other — have gathered separately in various places, O king.

sanskrit: idam abhyadhikaṃ rājan brāhmaṇā guravaś ca te sametāḥ kathayantīha muditāḥ satyasaṃdhatām
english: And this above all, O king: your elders and brahmins, assembled here, speak joyfully of your steadfastness to truth.

sanskrit: yan na mohān na kārpaṇyān na lobhān na bhayād api anṛtaṃ kiṃ cid uktaṃ te na kāmān nārthakāraṇāt
english: That you have spoken no falsehood — neither out of delusion, nor meanness, nor greed, nor fear, nor desire, nor for the sake of gain.

sanskrit: yad enaḥ kurute kiṃ cid rājā bhūmim avāpnuvan sarvaṃ tan nudate paścād yajñair vipuladakṣiṇaiḥ
english: Whatever sin a king incurs in the course of conquering the earth — all of that he afterwards washes away through sacrifices with generous fees.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇebhyo dadad grāmān gāś ca rājan sahasraśaḥ mucyate sarvapāpebhyas tamobhya iva candramāḥ
english: By giving villages and thousands of cows to brahmins, O king, one is freed from all sins — just as the moon is freed from darkness.

sanskrit: paurajānapadāḥ sarve prāyaśaḥ kurunandana savṛddhabālāḥ sahitāḥ śaṃsanti tvāṃ yudhiṣṭhira
english: All the citizens and countryfolk — young and old together — for the most part praise you, O Yudhiṣṭhira, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: śvadṛtau kṣīram āsaktaṃ brahma vā vṛṣale yathā satyaṃ stene balaṃ nāryāṃ rājyaṃ duryodhane tathā
english: As milk poured into a dog's skin, or the Veda lodged in a low-born man, as truth in a thief, as strength in a woman — so is kingship in Duryodhana.

sanskrit: iti nirvacanaṃ loke ciraṃ carati bhārata api caitat striyo bālāḥ svādhyāyam iva kurvate
english: This saying has long circulated in the world, O Bhārata; even women and children repeat it as though it were a sacred recitation.

sanskrit: sa bhavān ratham āsthāya sarvopakaraṇānvitam tvaramāṇo 'bhiniryātu ciram arthopapādakam
english: Therefore let Your Honour mount the chariot equipped with all accessories and march forth swiftly — to achieve long-awaited prosperity.

sanskrit: vācayitvā dvijaśreṣṭhān adyaiva gajasāhvayam astravidbhiḥ parivṛto bhrātṛbhir dṛḍhadhanvibhiḥ āśīviṣasamair vīrair marudbhir iva vṛtrahā
english: Having the foremost brahmins recite auspicious verses this very day, set out for Hāstinapura, surrounded by your brothers who are firm-bowed and skilled in weapons — heroes like venomous serpents, like Indra the slayer of Vṛtra surrounded by the Maruts.

sanskrit: amitrāṃs tejasā mṛdnann asurebhya ivārihā śriyam ādatsva kaunteya dhārtarāṣṭrān mahābala
english: Crushing your enemies with your splendour as Indra crushed the asuras, O son of Kuntī, O mighty one, reclaim your sovereignty from the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: na hi gāṇḍīvamuktānāṃ śarāṇāṃ gārdhravāsasām sparśam āśīviṣābhānāṃ martyaḥ kaś cana saṃsahet
english: No mortal can endure the touch of the arrows loosed from the Gāṇḍīva bow, feathered with vulture plumes and swift as venomous serpents.

sanskrit: na sa vīro na mātaṅgo na sadaśvo 'sti bhārata yaḥ saheta gadāvegaṃ mama kruddhasya saṃyuge
english: There is no hero, no elephant, no fine horse, O Bhārata, that could withstand the force of my mace when I am enraged in battle.

sanskrit: sṛñjayaiḥ saha kaikeyair vṛṣṇīnām ṛṣabheṇa ca kathaṃ svid yudhi kaunteya rājyaṃ na prāpnuyāmahe
english: With the Sṛñjayas, the Kekayas, and the bull of the Vṛṣṇis at our side, how could we not win back the kingdom in battle, O son of Kuntī?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca asaṃśayaṃ bhārata satyam etad; yan mā tudan vākyaśalyaiḥ kṣiṇoṣi na tvā vigarhe pratikūlam etan; mamānayād dhi vyasanaṃ va āgāt
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Undoubtedly, O Bhārata, what you say is true; by piercing me with the darts of your words you wear me down. I do not reproach you for this contrary speech — for this calamity came upon us through my own transgression.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hy akṣān anvapadyaṃ jihīrṣan; rājyaṃ sarāṣṭraṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāt tan mā śaṭhaḥ kitavaḥ pratyadevīt; suyodhanārthaṃ subalasya putraḥ
english: For I followed the dice, wishing to win back from Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son the kingdom with all its territory; but that rogue gambler — Subala's son, working for Suyodhana — played against me and defeated me.

sanskrit: mahāmāyaḥ śakuniḥ pārvatīyaḥ; sadā sabhāyāṃ pravapann akṣapūgān amāyinaṃ māyayā pratyadevīt; tato 'paśyaṃ vṛjinaṃ bhīmasena
english: That great illusionist Śakuni, the mountain prince, ever casting masses of dice in the assembly hall, defeated me — guileless as I was — by trickery; only then did I see the wrong of it, O Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: akṣān hi dṛṣṭvā śakuner yathāvat; kāmānulomān ayujo yujaś ca śakyaṃ niyantum abhaviṣyad ātmā; manyus tu hanti puruṣasya dhairyam
english: Had I truly seen Śakuni's dice for what they were — favouring desire, loaded and unloaded as he wished — my self-control might have been possible; but anger destroys a man's steadiness.

sanskrit: yantuṃ nātmā śakyate pauruṣeṇa; mānena vīryeṇa ca tāta naddhaḥ na te vācaṃ bhīmasenābhyasūye; manye tathā tad bhavitavyam āsīt
english: The self cannot be restrained by manhood, by pride, or by valour alone, dear one, when it is bound up in them. I do not blame your words, O Bhīmasena; I think that is how things were destined to be.

sanskrit: sa no rājā dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putro; nyapātayad vyasane rājyam icchan dāsyaṃ ca no 'gamayad bhīmasena; yatrābhavac charaṇaṃ draupadī naḥ
english: That son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, desiring kingship, plunged us into this calamity and brought us to servitude, O Bhīmasena — even Draupadī, who had been our refuge, was brought to that state.

sanskrit: tvaṃ cāpi tad vettha dhanaṃjayaś ca; punardyūtāyāgatānāṃ sabhāṃ naḥ yan mābravīd dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putra; ekaglahārthaṃ bharatānāṃ samakṣam
english: You know it, and so does Dhanaṃjaya — when we had come to the assembly hall for the second game of dice, what Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son said to me, before the Bharatas assembled, as a single stake.

sanskrit: vane samā dvādaśa rājaputra; yathākāmaṃ viditam ajātaśatro athāparaṃ cāviditaṃ carethāḥ; sarvaiḥ saha bhrātṛbhiś chadmagūḍhaḥ
english: "Twelve years in the forest, O prince — as you know, O Ajātaśatru — and then a thirteenth year, moving unrecognised, concealed, with all your brothers in disguise."

sanskrit: tvāṃ cec chrutvā tāta tathā carantam; avabhotsyante bhāratānāṃ carāḥ sma anyāṃś carethās tāvato 'bdāṃs tatas tvaṃ; niścitya tat pratijānīhi pārtha
english: "If the Bharatas' spies learn of your living thus, dear one, you shall live equally many more years concealed; having decided that, agree to it, O Pārtha."

sanskrit: caraiś cen no 'viditaḥ kālam etaṃ; yukto rājan mohayitvā madīyān bravīmi satyaṃ kurusaṃsadīha; tavaiva tā bhārata pañca nadyaḥ
english: "If you pass this period undiscovered by spies, O king, having baffled my agents with cunning — I speak the truth here in the Kuru assembly — those five rivers, O Bhārata, shall be yours."

sanskrit: vayaṃ caivaṃ bhrātaraḥ sarva eva; tvayā jitāḥ kālam apāsya bhogān vasema ity āha purā sa rājā; madhye kurūṇāṃ sa mayoktas tatheti
english: "And we, all brothers together, conquered by you — setting aside pleasures for the appointed time, we shall live thus" — so that king said before the Kurus. And I answered him: "So be it."

sanskrit: tatra dyūtam abhavan no jaghanyaṃ; tasmiñ jitāḥ pravrajitāś ca sarve itthaṃ ca deśān anusaṃcarāmo; vanāni kṛcchrāṇi ca kṛcchrarūpāḥ
english: Then there was that wretched second gambling match; defeated in it, all of us were banished. And so we wander through lands and through difficult forests in this distressed condition.

sanskrit: suyodhanaś cāpi na śāntim icchan; bhūyaḥ sa manyor vaśam anvagacchat udyojayām āsa kurūṃś ca sarvān; ye cāsya ke cid vaśam anvagacchan
english: And Suyodhana, desiring no peace, fell again under the sway of his anger and stirred up all the Kurus — and whoever else came under his influence.

sanskrit: taṃ saṃdhim āsthāya satāṃ sakāśe; ko nāma jahyād iha rājyahetoḥ āryasya manye maraṇād garīyo; yad dharmam utkramya mahīṃ praśiṣyāt
english: Having made that agreement in the presence of the good — who would break it now for the sake of kingship? I think it worse than death for a noble man to rule the earth by transgressing dharma.

sanskrit: tadaiva ced vīrakarmākariṣyo; yadā dyūte parighaṃ paryamṛkṣaḥ bāhū didhakṣan vāritaḥ phalgunena; kiṃ duṣkṛtaṃ bhīma tadābhaviṣyat
english: If you were going to do a heroic deed, you should have done it then — when in the gambling hall you reached for the iron bar, yearning to burn their arms, but were restrained by Phalguna. What wrong would there have been then, Bhīma?

sanskrit: prāg eva caivaṃ samayakriyāyāḥ; kiṃ nābravīḥ pauruṣam āvidānaḥ prāptaṃ tu kālaṃ tv abhipadya paścāt; kiṃ mām idānīm ativelam āttha
english: Why did you not declare your manhood before the agreement was made? But now, having let the appointed moment pass, why do you speak to me so excessively at this late hour?

sanskrit: bhūyo 'pi duḥkhaṃ mama bhīmasena; dūye viṣasyeva rasaṃ viditvā yad yājñasenīṃ parikṛṣyamāṇāṃ; saṃdṛśya tat kṣāntam iti sma bhīma
english: Even greater is my sorrow, O Bhīmasena — knowing in the dice hall the taste of poison itself — that I endured seeing Yājñasenī being dragged about. That is what was borne, O Bhīma.

sanskrit: na tv adya śakyaṃ bharatapravīra; kṛtvā yad uktaṃ kuruvīramadhye kālaṃ pratīkṣasva sukhodayasya; paktiṃ phalānām iva bījavāpaḥ
english: But what was declared before the midst of the Kuru heroes cannot be undone today, O foremost of the Bharatas; wait for the time of happiness to arise — like the sower of seeds waiting for the ripening of fruits.

sanskrit: yadā hi pūrvaṃ nikṛto nikṛtyā; vairaṃ sapuṣpaṃ saphalaṃ viditvā mahāguṇaṃ harati hi pauruṣeṇa; tadā vīro jīvati jīvaloke
english: For when one who has been previously wronged through treachery, knowing that enmity has flowered and fruited, takes full revenge through manly valour — then a hero truly lives in the world of the living.

sanskrit: śriyaṃ ca loke labhate samagrāṃ; manye cāsmai śatravaḥ saṃnamante mitrāṇi cainam atirāgād bhajante; devā ivendram anujīvanti cainam
english: And he attains full sovereignty in the world; I believe his enemies bow before him, his friends adore him with deep devotion, and they live in his service as the gods live in the service of Indra.

sanskrit: mama pratijñāṃ ca nibodha satyāṃ; vṛṇe dharmam amṛtāj jīvitāc ca rājyaṃ ca putrāś ca yaśo dhanaṃ ca; sarvaṃ na satyasya kalām upaiti
english: Know my vow, which is true: I choose dharma over immortality and over life itself; kingdom, sons, glory, wealth — all this does not equal even a fraction of truth.

sanskrit: bhīmasena uvāca saṃdhiṃ kṛtvaiva kālena antakena patatriṇā anantenāprameyena srotasā sarvahāriṇā
english: Bhīmasena said: Making a pact with Time — the destroyer, the swift-winged, the endless, the immeasurable, the current that sweeps all away —

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ manyase kālaṃ martyaḥ san kālabandhanaḥ phenadharmā mahārāja phaladharmā tathaiva ca
english: — you, a mortal bound by Time, think you can see Time directly? O great king, like foam it arises, and like fruit it falls.

sanskrit: nimeṣād api kaunteya yasyāyur apacīyate sūcyevāñjanacūrṇasya kim iti pratipālayet
english: He whose lifespan diminishes even by a blink of the eye — like collyrium powder falling from a needle's tip — why should he wait?

sanskrit: yo nūnam amitāyuḥ syād atha vāpi pramāṇavit sa kālaṃ vai pratīkṣeta sarvapratyakṣadarśivān
english: Only one who had unlimited life, or who truly knew its measure, who could see all things directly — only such a one might wait for the right time.

sanskrit: pratīkṣamāṇān kālo naḥ samā rājaṃs trayodaśa āyuṣo 'pacayaṃ kṛtvā maraṇāyopaneṣyati
english: While we wait, O king, Time — having consumed thirteen years of our lives — will bring us to death itself.

sanskrit: śarīriṇāṃ hi maraṇaṃ śarīre nityam āśritam prāg eva maraṇāt tasmād rājyāyaiva ghaṭāmahe
english: Death is ever lodged within the body of every embodied being; therefore, before death comes, let us strive for the kingdom itself.
